annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete local paper, compared every proposed tier candidate with the exact source and the frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines, rejected the non-source T1 and T2 formulations, and retained only the source-faithful T3 target.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P08 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the three stability definitions in section 2
rejected_candidates.reason: These introduce backward-error measures and stability terminology rather than proving finite conclusions.
The result is explicitly attributed to Oettli and Prager (1964), and its proof is delegated to prior work.

Their existential perturbation constructions depend on continuity across poles, infima, absolute norms, and explicit matrix inverses. The selected tasks retain the paper's later iterative-refinement contributions with more direct finite source anchors.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the basic Gaussian-elimination error estimate and equation (3.1)
rejected_candidates.reason: The basic estimate is taken from Skeel (1979); equation (3.1) is background used by the new refinement analysis.
The theorem is a direct substitution of Lemma 4.3 into Lemma 4.2 and introduces further anonymous constants; the full Lemma 4.3 target preserves the substantive finite recurrence.
These use informal limits and anonymous constants; the finite recurrence certificate in T3 avoids an unstated convergence formalization.
The displayed bounds are explicitly derived from external theorems in Jankowski and Wozniakowski (1977).

The full formulas combine anonymous constants, asymptotic interpretation, and Theorems 2.2 and 4.4. The retained Lemma 4.3 task preserves the exact finite iterative-refinement recurrence without encoding O(u^2).
The counterexample text is partially degraded in the supplied scan and the surrounding row-pivoting bounds are stated as straightforward modifications rather than separately proved results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the complete unlabelled one-refinement identity on printed page 825
rejected_candidates.reason: Rejected after strict source audit. The discarded P08-T2 changed the paper's sign convention and specialized the nonzero rounded-update term h2 to zero; that produced an artificial theorem rather than a faithful formalization of the displayed four-step argument.

rejected_candidates.candidate: a gamma_(n+1) conventional-residual theorem extracted from equation (4.1)
rejected_candidates.reason: Rejected after strict source audit. The paper states a different precision-sensitive bound involving n*ubar+c3*u^2 and u+c4*u^2. The gamma_(n+1) theorem is a valid nearby result, but it is not the statement proved in this paper.

T1.decision: Skipped after strict source audit: the paper's equation (4.1) uses its own single- and double-precision residual bounds and constants c3 and c4. The available NumStability conventional-residual theorem states a different modern gamma_(n+1) bound, so using it would create a related but non-source T1 task.

T2.decision: Skipped after strict source audit: the candidate changed Ax-b and x-d to b-Ax and x+d and removed the rounded update h2. The paper's actual Lemma 4.1 can be stated faithfully, but the available library results do not directly supply its precision-sensitive residual model, so no genuine two-result T2 remains.

T3.decision: Use the complete algorithm-linked Lemma 4.3 componentwise bound, preserving q_(m+1), exponent m, the precision-sensitive four terms, source constants, conditioning threshold, recurrence, and q_1 base case.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject definitions, experiments, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds, identities, and the finite recurrence behind an induction.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
